title: Leclerc fastest in Mexico FP1 as new faces make F1 debuts
excerpt:
Charles Leclerc finished fastest in Free Practice 1 ahead of the Mexico City Grand Prix, the Ferrari driver heading Kimi Antonelli and Fred Vesti.

Leclerc posted a 1m 18.128s which left him 0.659s clear of Antonelli at the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez, with the second Mercedes in the hands of Vesti – in place of George Russell for FP1 – just one-tenth further back.

Plenty of new faces headed out on track once the green light appeared at the end of the pit lane for the opening hour of practice at 1230 local time, with 10 out of 11 teams running young drivers and only Ferrari keeping its regular line-up.

This included F1 debuts for Red Bull junior and Formula 2 frontrunner Nikola Tsolov, driving Liam Lawson's Racing Bulls, as well as Audi development driver and Formula 3 runner-up, Freddie Slater, at the wheel of Gabriel Bortoleto's car.

Grip was at a premium in the early running due to the dusty track surface, with Antonelli, who stands on the cusp of his maiden drivers' title this weekend, sliding his way through the stadium section, as did home hero Sergio Perez.

Isack Hadjar had to coast his Red Bull back the pits due to a power unit issue approaching the 10-minute mark, with Leclerc becoming the first to dip below the 1m 20s barrier shortly after with a 1m 19.197s on the hard Pirelli tyre.

Nico Hulkenberg suffered a heavy lock-up and took to the run-off area at Turn 1, Arvid Lindblad ran wide at Turn 12 heading into the stadium section, while reigning F2 champion Leonardo Fornaroli – in for Lando Norris at McLaren – recovered from a huge slide exiting Turn 11.

Oscar Piastri in the second McLaren also went deep at Turn 1 and cut across the grass, with drivers pushing the limits at a venue where the thin air – the track located more than 2000 metres above sea level – makes a big difference.

Slater's F1 debut was compromised at the halfway point of the session, Audi having sent the young Briton out on track with a sidepod fan still attached to the car which appeared to cause some damage to the power unit and left him in the pits for a prolonged period. The stewards are set to investigate the unsafe release post-session.

By this point drivers and teams began to use the soft tyre, Leclerc posting a 1m 18.128s on his first effort with the red-walled tyre, with Antonelli more than six tenths further back.

A brief Virtual Safety Car was deployed approaching the final 10 minutes as Jak Crawford – in for Lance Stroll – brought his Aston Martin to a stop at Turn 1 with a problem.

Leclerc remained fastest at the chequered flag from Antonelli and Vesti, with Ferrari team mate Lewis Hamilton seven tenths adrift.

The top 10 was completed by Ayumu Iwasa (replacing Max Verstappen at Red Bull), Pierre Gasly (Alpine), Fernando Alonso's Aston Martin, Piastri, the Haas of Bearman and Lindblad's Racing Bulls.

Hadjar recovered to P11 after his earlier problem, from Tsolov, Hulkenberg and F2 race winner Gabriele Mini, who was also making his F1 debut in Franco Colapinto's Alpine.

Ryo Hirakawa (driving Esteban Ocon's Haas) was P15, with the order completed by Carlos Sainz (Williams), Fornaroli, Perez, Crawford, Luke Browning (driving Alex Albon's Williams), Slater and Colton Herta (in Valtteri Bottas' Cadillac).

title: 7 memorable FP1 debuts from future F1 stars
excerpt:
Freddie Slater and Nikola Tsolov will take another significant step up the motorsport ladder at the Mexico City Grand Prix, as they make their FP1 debuts for Audi and Racing Bulls.

The pair feature in a bumper group of young drivers getting Formula 1 track time on Friday, with Fred Vesti, Leonardo Fornaroli, Jak Crawford, Luke Browning and Colton Herta also getting behind the wheel for Mercedes, McLaren, Aston Martin, Williams and Cadillac respectively.

And plenty of future F1 stars have made their mark in Friday practice before them. F1.com looks back at some familiar names who made FP1 performances...

Kimi Antonelli – Italy 2024

Kimi Antonelli stands on the cusp of the drivers' title this weekend in Mexico City, which would make him the youngest driver to achieve the feat in the championship's history.

It's even more remarkable given that his first appearance on an F1 weekend came only just over two years ago.

Ahead of the 2024 Italian Grand Prix, Antonelli was thrust into the limelight in front of his home fans as he was handed George Russell's Mercedes for FP1.

Anticipation around the Italian, who had only just turned 18, had continued to grow since Mercedes signed him to their development programme several years earlier and fast-tracked him through the junior categories.

For the then-F2 driver, his F1 weekend debut began in spectacular fashion as he set the fastest time before crashing at the Parabolica after only 10 minutes.

A further FP1 outing came in Mexico, having been announced just a day after his Monza crash as Lewis Hamilton's replacement at Mercedes for 2025.

After a rollercoaster rookie season that yielded three podiums, Antonelli has asserted himself in 2026, with nine wins leaving him on the brink of history.

Lando Norris – Belgium 2018

The reigning World Champion has only ever raced with McLaren since making his F1 debut in 2019, so it's unsurprising that Lando Norris' first appearance in F1 came with the Woking-based team.

Norris was still racing in F2 at the time, having claimed the European F3 title the previous season. He would eventually finish runner-up to George Russell, but during the campaign was handed Fernando Alonso's McLaren for FP1 at the 2018 Belgian Grand Prix.

Norris finished P18, one place ahead of regular driver Stoffel Vandoorne, before being handed six further Friday outings ahead of a full-time drive in 2019.

Helping McLaren move up the grid over several seasons, Norris claimed his maiden F1 victory at the 2024 Miami Grand Prix before securing last year's Drivers' title by two points from Max Verstappen.

George Russell – Brazil 2017

Having been signed by Mercedes as a junior driver in 2017, it didn't take long for George Russell to have his first experience of modern F1 machinery.

The Briton was handed his first FP1 opportunity with Force India, a Mercedes engine customer team, ahead of the 2017 Brazilian Grand Prix having already secured that year's GP3 title.

Setting the 12th-fastest time, Russell was given another chance ahead of the final round in Abu Dhabi, finishing FP1 in P11.

After securing the F2 title at his first attempt in 2018, Russell was handed a full-time F1 seat with Williams. He spent three seasons there before stepping up to Mercedes in 2022.

Charles Leclerc – Great Britain 2016

Charles Leclerc joined the Ferrari Driver Academy in 2016 on his way to securing the GP3 Series title, while also making several FP1 appearances for Haas.

His first appearance came ahead of the British Grand Prix, where the Monegasque driver finished P18 before taking part in a further three FP1 sessions over the remainder of the season.

More Friday running followed with Sauber in 2017 as Leclerc dominated the F2 campaign, before a full-time F1 seat beckoned with the team in 2018.

An impressive rookie season earned him a move to Ferrari for 2019, replacing Kimi Raikkonen. Leclerc won in Belgium and Italy during his first campaign for the Scuderia, while his most recent victory came at Silverstone earlier this year.

Max Verstappen – Japan 2014

There was huge anticipation around Max Verstappen's first F1 appearance following a meteoric rise through the ranks, which included just one season of single-seater racing in European F3.

The son of former F1 driver Jos Verstappen, the Dutchman became the youngest driver to appear in F1, having only just turned 17, when he made his first appearance for Toro Rosso ahead of the 2014 Japanese Grand Prix.

After finishing P12, Verstappen was given two more Friday outings before the end of the season ahead of stepping up to a race seat with Toro Rosso for 2015.

After completing his rookie season with Toro Rosso, Verstappen was promoted to Red Bull just four races into the 2016 campaign. He won on his debut with the team at the Spanish Grand Prix before going on to claim four consecutive Drivers' titles from 2021 to 2024.

Sebastian Vettel – Turkey 2006

Sebastian Vettel quickly began to make a name for himself in the junior categories, securing the 2004 Formula BMW ADAC championship with 18 wins from 20 races before a solid campaign in the Formula 3 Euro Series.

With support from BMW, Vettel was handed a Williams F1 test, but his first Grand Prix weekend appearance came with BMW Sauber in Friday practice at the 2006 Turkish Grand Prix. Four more Friday outings followed.

Becoming BMW Sauber's test driver for the 2007 season, Vettel was handed his race debut at the United States Grand Prix in place of the injured Robert Kubica before joining Toro Rosso later that season.

Vettel delivered a stunning wet-weather victory for Toro Rosso at the 2008 Italian Grand Prix before stepping up to Red Bull the following season. Four consecutive drivers' titles followed between 2010 and 2013.

Title tilts and race wins followed over several seasons at Ferrari, before the German ended his career after a spell with Aston Martin.

Robert Kubica – Bahrain 2006

After claiming the 2005 Formula Renault 3.5 Series title, Robert Kubica earned an end-of-season test with reigning F1 world champions Renault in Barcelona, where his performance caught the eye of BMW Sauber.

The Pole, who had beaten the likes of Lewis Hamilton and Nico Rosberg through the karting ranks, became the team's official reserve driver and made his F1 weekend debut on Friday at the opening round of the season in Bahrain.

After setting the fastest time in the opening session, Kubica continued to impress, culminating in him replacing 1997 F1 drivers' champion Jacques Villeneuve at the 2006 Hungarian Grand Prix, with a podium following just two races later in Italy.

Kubica's sole F1 victory came at the 2008 Canadian Grand Prix – a result which put him at the top of the drivers' standings at the time – before he joined Renault in 2010.

A pre-season rally crash in 2011 nearly ended his career at a time when he had reportedly agreed a deal to join Ferrari for 2012.

After years of recovery, Kubica made a comeback with Williams in 2019 during a difficult spell for the team, before two one-off appearances for Alfa Romeo in 2021 brought his F1 racing career to an end.

Kubica now competes in the World Endurance Championship, his career renaissance culminating in victory at the 2025 24 Hours of Le Mans aboard the #83 AF Corse Ferrari 499P.

title: Which rookies are getting FP1 outings in Mexico?
excerpt:
Nearly every F1 team will field a rookie driver during Friday’s opening practice session for the Mexico City Grand Prix, with Ferrari the only outfit not to alter their line-up.

Just like in 2025, the regulations mandate that every full-time racer must make way for a rookie – viewed as someone who has started no more than two Grands Prix – in two practice sessions across the season.

But who exactly will be out on track? From experienced reserve drivers to those preparing to make their debut, here’s an overview of the 10 rookies set to make a Friday appearance…

Fred Vesti – Mercedes

Since becoming a Mercedes junior in 2021, Fred Vesti has made his way up to the role of third driver, in which he carries out crucial work on the simulator to support Kimi Antonelli and George Russell.

He is also no stranger to FP1 sessions, having appeared for the team at this season’s Barcelona-Catalunya and Hungarian Grands Prix, building on the experience he’s gained through his numerous outings – the first of which came in 2023.

After stepping in for championship leader Antonelli in Hungary, Vesti will replace Russell for the opening 60-minute session at the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez.

Ayumu Iwasa – Red Bull

Ayumu Iwasa is enjoying a busy season as he balances a Super Formula campaign – in which he is the reigning champion after winning the 2025 title – with his duties as Racing Bulls’ test and reserve driver.

Due to the team’s intrinsic connection to Red Bull, the Japanese racer has received FP1 opportunities at both outfits, spread across Barcelona, Austria, Italy and Mexico City this year alone.

Just as in Italy, Iwasa will get behind the wheel of Max Verstappen’s RB22 and give the Dutchman some catching up to do later in the weekend, but with five wins at this track under his belt, it’s clearly a happy hunting ground for the driver chasing P2 in the standings.

7 memorable FP1 debuts from future F1 stars

Leonardo Fornaroli – McLaren

Leonardo Fornaroli joined McLaren’s Driver Development Programme fresh off the back of his triumphant F2 season in 2025, and has made plenty of appearances for the defending Teams’ Champions since.

He took part in a Testing of Previous Cars (TPC) weekend earlier this month at France’s Circuit Paul Ricard, marking his sixth F1 test with the team, and will undertake back-to-back FP1 sessions in Mexico City and Sao Paulo.

The 21-year-old, who previously finished an eye-catching fifth in FP1 at the Barcelona-Catalunya Grand Prix, will take Lando Norris’ place as he continues to learn the intricacies of the MCL40.

Nikola Tsolov – Racing Bulls

The first new name on this list, Nikola Tsolov will make what could be an important first F1 appearance for Racing Bulls, with the team still yet to announce their driver line-up for the 2027 season.

Tsolov is a highly rated talent and sits just seven points off the lead of the F2 standings, but has only driven in showruns and a TPC test at Imola since signing for the Red Bull Junior Team in 2025.

Racing Bulls Team Principal Alan Permane has made it clear that they’re weighing the 19-year-old up against current drivers Liam Lawson and Arvid Lindblad, so Tsolov has a chance to impress when he replaces the former in Friday's FP1 session.

Why Tsolov has complicated Racing Bulls' 2027 plans

Gabriele Mini – Alpine

Gabriele Mini is another F2 driver making his debut this weekend, having been a member of the Alpine Academy since 2023 when he made the transition from Formula Regional to F3.

After finishing seventh in his first season, the Italian finished as runner-up in 2024 before embarking on a trio of campaigns in F2 – he’s now fourth in the standings with two victories and a further seven podiums.

While reserve driver Paul Aron has been given the bulk of FP1 opportunities by Alpine this year, it’s Mini who will jump in the cockpit of Franco Colapinto’s A526 in Mexico City.

Ryo Hirakawa – Haas

Although Haas have signed Ferrari junior Rafael Camara for 2027, veteran racer Ryo Hirakawa will drive in FP1 for the third time this season, having stepped in at the Red Bull Ring and Hungaroring.

On top of his responsibilities as the American squad’s test and reserve driver, the 32-year-old has built an impressive career with Toyota in the World Endurance Championship.

Esteban Ocon, who will depart Haas at the end of the year, will make way for Hirakawa in the first hour of practice this weekend.

Freddie Slater – Audi

Freddie Slater, the very first member of Audi's Driver Development Programme, is another rising star and will get his first taste of F1 machinery at the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez.

After the 18-year-old narrowly missed out on the F3 title, it was confirmed that he will progress to F2 next season, leading Audi Racing Director Allan McNish to declare that “it is the right time for Freddie to step up”.

Like Fornaroli, he will drive in both Mexico City and Sao Paulo, hopping into Gabriel Bortoleto’s R26 on this occasion.

Why Audi's DDP is about more than their next F1 star

Luke Browning – Williams

Like Iwasa, Luke Browning is driving in Super Formula alongside his role as reserve driver for Williams, which has seen him offered FP1 drives in Barcelona, Austria, Italy, Mexico City and Sao Paulo.

Teams usually set aside four practice sessions for rookie drivers as per the regulations, but in Browning’s case, the Grove-based outfit gave him one extra after an electrical issue prevented him from heading out on track at the Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya.

The 24-year-old finished in P15 just above Carlos Sainz at Monza and will once again take over Alex Albon’s FW48 this weekend.

Jak Crawford – Aston Martin

A year on from his free practice debut in Mexico City, Aston Martin’s reserve driver Jak Crawford will return to the track and take Lance Stroll’s seat.

It will mark his final FP1 appearance of the season after outings in Japan, Austria – where he took his highest finish of P20, placing above Sergio Perez and Fernando Alonso – and Belgium.

Colton Herta – Cadillac

American driver Colton Herta will participate in his fifth practice session of the year for Cadillac as he edges closer towards securing his Super Licence, which he will achieve if he completes at least 100km of running on Friday.

That could make him a serious candidate for a future seat at the team, especially when combined with his experience in IndyCar and F2. As it stands, he’s 19th in the latter, but it’s understood that he impressed Cadillac during prior FP1 outings in Barcelona, Hungary and the United States.

Another planned drive in Italy was limited to five laps due to technical issues, but Herta will have a chance to finish the laps he needs when he takes the wheel of Valtteri Bottas’ MAC-26.

title: Midfield fight on a ‘knife’s edge’ as Audi target Haas
excerpt:
Nico Hulkenberg believes Audi must be “flawless” to capitalise on opportunities in the tightly contested midfield battle this weekend in Mexico, while team mate Gabriel Bortoleto remains confident the squad can close the gap to Haas in the teams' standings.

Audi head into the Mexico City Grand Prix looking to turn their recent competitiveness into valuable points, having narrowly missed out on the top 10 at the United States Grand Prix last weekend.

Hulkenberg recovered to finish 11th in Austin after an anti-stall issue at the start cost him several positions, while team mate Bortoleto climbed to 13th from the back of the grid following penalties for taking on new power unit components.

With Audi sitting eighth in the teams’ standings, seven points behind Haas, both drivers believe there are opportunities to make further progress in the remaining five rounds of the season.

Speaking on Thursday's media day in Mexico, Hulkenberg acknowledged that the increasingly competitive midfield leaves little room for error, with the German having finished 11th in three of the last four Grands Prix.

“I think we’re in striking distance, but we need to be flawless,” he said. “We need to be very clean, us drivers on the driving side and the team on the operational side, to really get those results.

“Otherwise, we’ll just be missing out. It’s really on a knife’s edge, usually with the Racing Bulls and the Alpines. So we go down to the wire, but it’s all to play for. The competition is high, and we’re ready for what’s to come.

"There is more on the table. Every weekend there are opportunities, and it’s our job to grab them and capitalise on them. I think our package is competitive, but we need to be clean and make no mistakes. The car needs to hold up... But if we stay clean, I think we’re in the fight for points.”

Bortoleto was similarly encouraged by Audi’s recent performance at the Circuit of The Americas, having shown top-10 pace throughout much of the weekend before his grid penalty left him facing an uphill battle on Sunday.

All the stories that got the Mexico City paddock talking

“Austin was very positive. Since FP1, I felt amazing with the car. We were inside the top 10 for most of the sessions,” said the Brazilian driver.

“We were super competitive. I felt so good when I finished that lap in Q1... At the same time, you leave the weekend believing there was an opportunity to be in the points, which we didn’t manage to achieve because of where I was starting. But it’s part of the game. We had to take the penalty, and now we move on. No penalty here, so hopefully I can have a good race.

“I’m looking forward to racing here. Last year, it gave me one point, so it’s a good track. Obviously, the long straights for us are a little bit of a pain, but we’re going to give our best. We’ll try to put in a good lap in Qualifying, have good pace in the race and hopefully deliver some points.

When asked about catching Haas in the Constructors' Championship, Bortoleto added: "We have five races to go, and we have good pace in most of these races. I think at some of them we may struggle a little bit more or less than at others, but I really believe we can achieve that."

title: The greatest pranks in Formula 1 history
excerpt:
Formula 1 drivers are used to keeping their rivals on their toes, but sometimes the biggest surprises happen away from the circuit. From team radio trickery to elaborate practical jokes years in the making, the paddock has never been short of mischief.

And while today's grid has plenty of pranksters, it is a tradition stretching back decades, with even some of the sport's greatest World Champions getting involved. With Halloween approaching, we revisit some of F1's most memorable practical jokes.

The team mates who just can't help themselves

Few Formula 1 partnerships have produced quite as many practical jokes as Ayrton Senna and Gerhard Berger's time together at McLaren between 1990 and 1992.

The Austrian was notorious for his mischievous sense of humour, and Senna frequently found himself on the receiving end. Their friendship produced several legendary stories, but perhaps the most memorable involved a trip to Australia, a hotel room and approximately 50 frogs.

After spotting frogs on a golf course during an evening run, Berger enlisted the help of a hotel concierge to collect them, reportedly handing over $100 for the favour. With the assistance of Ron Dennis' wife Lisa, Berger then scattered the frogs throughout Senna's room while the Brazilian was out at dinner.

When a furious Senna confronted his team mate the following morning, Berger had one more trick up his sleeve, asking if he had found the snake yet!

Fortunately for Senna, the snake didn't actually exist.

That wasn't the end of their antics, either. Berger also famously replaced Senna's passport photograph with an inappropriate image and once threw his supposedly indestructible briefcase out of a helicopter. Senna eventually retaliated by filling Berger's shoes with shaving foam.

Decades later, Ferrari teammates Charles Leclerc and Carlos Sainz developed their own entertaining partnership, although their pranks tended to be considerably less elaborate.

For Sainz' 28th birthday in September 2022, Leclerc spent around 15 minutes squeezed inside a cupboard in his team mate's driver room, waiting for the perfect opportunity to jump out and surprise him.

The plan worked, with an unsuspecting Sainz opening the cupboard to find Leclerc bursting out with confetti. Unfortunately, some of it also landed in the birthday boy's coffee.

At least Charles remembered his birthday!

When even the press conferences aren't safe

An FIA press conference might not seem like the obvious location for a practical joke, but Michael Schumacher and Sebastian Vettel proved otherwise at the 2012 German Grand Prix.

As Nico Rosberg attempted to answer a question, the two former World Champions noticed that his microphone was considerably louder than everyone else's.

Rather than alerting him to the problem, Schumacher encouraged Vettel to move Rosberg's microphone even closer to his mouth.

The result was an increasingly distorted answer as Rosberg spoke on, with the drivers around him struggling to contain their laughter.

And they weren't the only drivers to cause chaos during interviews. Following the 1999 Canadian Grand Prix, Eddie Irvine interrupted Mika Hakkinen's post-race interviews by throwing a towel at the McLaren driver, sparking an escalating exchange involving water.

Radio silence? Not quite...

There are few messages an engineer wants to hear less than a driver suddenly announcing an engine problem in the closing stages of a Grand Prix.

At the 2011 Japanese Grand Prix, Sergio Perez decided to use exactly that scenario for a joke.

The Sauber driver had started the race in 17th but produced an impressive recovery drive to climb into eighth, putting him on course for a valuable points finish. Then, on the final lap, Perez radioed his team to announce that he had no power.

His race engineer Marco Schupbach urged him to keep pushing towards the finish, only for Perez to reveal, after crossing the line, that the entire thing had been a joke.

Fortunately, Schupbach was quick to get his revenge!

The engineer told Perez that his teammate Kamui Kobayashi had finished fourth, despite actually crossing the line in 13th. The Mexican was completely taken in, repeatedly questioning the result before Schupbach revealed that he had been pranked in return.

And their practical jokes didn't stop there. Ahead of the 2012 Belgian Grand Prix, Schupbach enlisted the help of the Sauber team, including Kobayashi, for an elaborate revenge prank. Convincing Perez he was testing new wet-weather technology, they fitted a fake rain button to his steering wheel, leaving the Mexican puzzled by the supposed innovation. The entire encounter was secretly filmed, giving the team the last laugh nearly a year after his original radio prank.

Antonelli versus Bono: The Mercedes prank war

Kimi Antonelli might be fighting for the World Championship in 2026, but that hasn't stopped the Mercedes driver waging a rather different battle against his race engineer, Peter 'Bono' Bonnington.

It began during 2025 pre-season testing in Bahrain, when Antonelli celebrated Bono's birthday by pushing a plate of cream cake into his face. A year later, the Italian returned armed with a powerful water pistol, chasing his engineer through the paddock and even attracting the attention of Bono's former driver and seven-time World Champion, Lewis Hamilton.

Bono wasn't going down without a fight, threatening Antonelli with a fire extinguisher before getting his revenge by secretly adding hot sauce to the youngster's water bottle.

By May, Antonelli had taken his antics back to Mercedes HQ in Brackley, arranging for Bono's security pass to be deactivated. When the engineer found himself locked out, he immediately suspected the culprit to be the young Italian!

The tables eventually turned at the Italian Grand Prix in September, when a group of Mercedes mechanics ambushed Antonelli with plates of whipped cream to celebrate his 20th birthday, some wearing protective ponchos for the occasion.

But there is one person Antonelli hasn't dared to prank just yet – Team Principal Toto Wolff. Speaking in October, the Italian admitted that targeting his boss would require considerably more courage, but a successful championship campaign might finally give him an excuse!

A seat at the table for George Russell

When the drivers gathered for their traditional end-of-season dinner ahead of the 2024 Abu Dhabi Grand Prix, tensions between Max Verstappen and George Russell were already making headlines.

After the pair clashed during the previous race weekend in Qatar, the rest of the grid spotted an opportunity for some entertainment.

Naturally, the rest of the grid spotted an opportunity for some entertainment.

As Liam Lawson later explained on an F1 podcast, the drivers deliberately filled the seats around the dinner table while keeping a place free beside Verstappen for the late-arriving Russell.

When Russell finally appeared, Verstappen cheerfully informed him that they had saved him a seat!

Unfortunately for the pranksters, Russell wasn't prepared to play along. Rather than take the offered spot, he simply picked up the chair, carried it to the opposite end of the table and sat alongside his then-Mercedes teammate Lewis Hamilton.

Lawson later admitted the group had found the entire situation hilarious, even if their intended victim hadn't been quite so amused!

An ear-resistible prank

Returning to the scene of his 1976 Nurburgring accident might have seemed an unlikely setting for a practical joke, but Niki Lauda had other ideas.

In 2013, ahead of the release of Rush, the film depicting his rivalry with James Hunt, Lauda returned to the Nurburgring with an American television crew.

As the three-time World Champion discussed his infamous 1976 accident, in which he suffered severe burns and injuries, he suddenly bent down and retrieved something lying in the grass.

Holding it up, Lauda jokingly announced that he had discovered his missing ear.

The horrified reaction was exactly what he had hoped for. The object was actually a biscuit that Lauda had discreetly placed on the ground beforehand, allowing him to turn a serious interview into an unforgettable practical joke.

The next generation of paddock pranksters

The 2026 grid has provided its own share of practical jokes, particularly at Racing Bulls, where Liam Lawson and Arvid Lindblad have been getting creative with their attempts to embarrass one another.

In October, Lawson teamed up with Sky Sports F1 presenters Simon Lazenby and Naomi Schiff to trick his rookie team mate into taking part in a staged television interview, completely unaware that the whole thing had been arranged as a prank.

But Lindblad soon had his revenge. With the help of a hidden earpiece, he turned Lawson into an unsuspecting participant in a series of challenges around the paddock, directing his team mate through the experience and putting him in some rather uncomfortable situations, including stealing Charles Leclerc’s microphone mid-interview.

And the McLaren drivers aren't immune to a little mischief either. During a media day karting challenge at Silverstone in July, Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri took control of a two-person kart, with Norris operating the pedals and Piastri steering.

But after the challenge ended, Norris decided to accelerate away with his unsuspecting team mate still aboard, leaving Piastri unable to do much other than hold on for the ride, even losing his hat in the process.

More than three decades after Berger was sneaking frogs into Senna's hotel room, F1's tradition of practical jokes is still going strong.

And with Halloween approaching, a few drivers might want to keep an especially close eye on their team mates...

title: Sauber veteran Zehnder to leave Audi at end of 2026
excerpt:
Veteran Swiss engineer and long-time Sauber Team Manager Beat Zehnder will leave the Formula 1 team now known as Audi at the end of the year.

The 60-year-old joined Sauber Motorsport in 1988, five years before the operation entered Formula 1, and won the 24 Hours of Le Mans and World Sportscar Championship with Sauber's sportscar programme.

He was there on the first day the Formula 1 team opened its doors in 1993 and stepped up to Team Manager the following year before being appointed to the management committee in 2018.

The Swiss worked on 601 consecutive Grands Prix and will have spent nearly four decades with the Hinwil-based squad.

During his time at the team, he has worked with the likes of world champions Kimi Raikkonen and Sebastian Vettel, plus race winners Charles Leclerc, Sergio Perez, Robert Kubica, Felipe Massa and Heinz-Harald Frentzen.

When Audi made Sauber their works team, he moved into a factory-based role, leading Audi's heritage activities as Director of Signature Programs and Operations.

On Friday, ahead of the Mexican Grand Prix weekend, Audi said Zehnder will leave the organisation "following the restructuring of its operations ahead of the 2027 season".

They added: "Beat has been a mentor to hundreds of team members and drivers who have passed through Hinwil over the years.

"During his tenure, he enjoyed both the highs and lows of working in such a demanding sport, never losing his professionalism, his relentless competitive streak and desire to win.

"We thank him for 39 years of outstanding service and wish him all the very best for the future."

title: Bearman offers update on F1 future ahead of Mexico City GP
excerpt:
Ollie Bearman has confirmed ahead of this weekend's Mexico City Grand Prix that "it's very clear I want to continue with Haas" in 2027, although no official announcement has yet been made.

Earlier this month Haas confirmed that Esteban Ocon would be replaced by Ferrari junior and current Formula 2 points leader Rafael Camara, the Brazilian expected to partner Bearman.

But Bearman's future has yet to be announced, with the Briton coming to the end of his second season with the American outfit.

"I think it's very clear I want to continue with Haas and that's definitely my goal," said Bearman during Thursday's media day in Mexico City.

"There's a few things in the background that we're working on but it's been very clear that continuing with Haas will be my target and we're just finalising a few things on that front."

When asked when any announcement would be coming, Bearman replied: "I don't know to be honest.

"It's not really in my hands, I can tell you that. If it was up to me, it would already have been announced a long time ago but there are a few bigger picture things that we're working on."

Bearman sits P13 in the drivers' standings, 16 points clear of Ocon, and arriving at a venue this weekend where he claimed his best finish in F1 with a fourth place.

Having lost his seat for 2027, Ocon confirmed in Mexico that discussions were still ongoing with a view to keeping him on the grid, with the second seat at Cadillac alongside Sergio Perez a possible option.

"I'm not going to really comment on the discussions I've had with teams in general," said Ocon when asked about the Cadillac rumours.

"Of course, we are talking with a lot of people on the grid at the moment. I feel like I have unfinished business in F1. I'm still very young, I still have a lot of things to achieve and that's where I want to be in the future."

title: Ultra-rare Ayrton Senna 1994 F1 Williams set for multi-million pound auction
excerpt:
A 1994 Williams F1 car driven by Ayrton Senna is to be auctioned next month - one of just two surviving FW16s the Brazilian drove.

FW16 chassis 01 was driven by Senna during pre-season testing and during the morning warm-up ahead of the 1994 Brazilian GP before he reverted to a different chassis for the race.

Senna was killed during the third race of the season, at the San Marino Grand Prix, driving chassis 02, which was later returned to Williams, and is believed to have been destroyed.

Chassis 01 was gifted to the Senna family at the end of 1994 as per a clause in Senna's contract which stated he was to be gifted an example of the FW16 if the team won the constructors' championship title - which it did after beating Benetton.

After Senna's death, FW16 chassis 01 was used as the spare car for Damon Hill in Monaco, before David Coulthard made his debut in the chassis at the Spanish GP in Barcelona.

The chassis was then used by Nigel Mansell during his comeback at the French GP, and was also driven by Coulthard in the British GP before it became a test machine or was used as the spare car, including for Hill in Japan and the title-deciding Australian GP.

The machine is to be auctioned next month in New York by RM Sotheby's, with an estimate of £2.950 million GBP to £4.450 million.

title: Max Verstappen booted from F1 podium after Sebastian Vettel rage
excerpt:
One of the more dramatic incidents that occurred in Mexico City took place 10 years ago today, between Max Verstappen and Sebastian Vettel.

Ten years ago today, Max Verstappen and Sebastian Vettel came to blows as they battled for the final spot on the podium at the Mexican Grand Prix.

In the late stages of the race, Verstappen was running in third place but had Vettel hounding him from behind, who in turn, was being chased by the second Red Bull of Daniel Ricciardo.

Ahead of the trio, the race was being controlled by Mercedes as Lewis Hamilton was on course for his 51st career win ahead of team-mate Nico Rosberg.

But the story of the afternoon was unfolding behind them.

On lap 68, Verstappen locked his brakes under pressure, cut across the grass through Turn 1 and Turn 2, and rejoined ahead of the Ferrari without giving the place back.

Ferrari immediately told Vettel over the radio that Verstappen needed to concede the position, but he never did.

[Article continues below]

Vettel's radio rant

Vettel's frustration spilt over on team radio, as he demanded Red Bull's driver be forced to move.

"Move! Move, for fuck's sake! He's a bastard, that's what he is," Vettel said over team radio.

"He has to give me the position. End of the story."

When told the stewards would not act immediately, Vettel aimed his fury at race director Charlie Whiting.

"Here's the message for Charlie: fuck off! Honestly. Fuck off!"

Vettel also accused Verstappen of deliberately backing him into Daniel Ricciardo's Red Bull, triggering wheel-to-wheel contact between the pair into Turn 4.

Verstappen crossed the line third and headed into the cool-down room, only to be pulled out before the podium ceremony once the stewards handed him a five-second penalty for leaving the track and gaining a lasting advantage.

That promoted Vettel onto the podium.

[Article continues below]

Penalty chaos and a late twist

Verstappen was scathing about the decision afterwards, drawing a comparison with unpunished incidents involving Hamilton and Rosberg earlier in the race.

"It is ridiculous,” he said. “I think that this is the same as in Turn 1. Hamilton exceeded the track limits and gained a lot of advantage.

“Rosberg also went off track when we ran into each other and even he gained an advantage. If they don't penalise them, they shouldn't penalise me either.”

He also had a dig at Vettel's radio outburst, stating: "Sebastian just starts shouting on the radio, using very bad language. I think he has to go back to school or something."

Hours later, the stewards reversed the podium again, hitting Vettel with a 10-second penalty for moving under braking against Ricciardo.

That dropped the German to fifth, demoted Verstappen to fourth, and finally confirmed Ricciardo as the true third-place finisher.

“For me he doesn't deserve to be up there with the move he pulled," Ricciardo said afterwards.

title: Charles Leclerc sends ominous message as Colton Herta takes huge step towards F1 in Mexico FP1
excerpt:
Charles Leclerc was quickest in FP1 at the Mexico City Grand Prix, but the most significant running went to Colton Herta at Cadillac.

30 October 8:35PM

Charles Leclerc topped the first free practice session at the Mexico City Grand Prix, going six-and-a-half tenths quicker than Kimi Antonelli in second.

Fred Vesti, in place of George Russell, was third-fastest at the Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez, ahead of Lewis Hamilton and Ayumu Iwasa, who was deputising for Max Verstappen.

The Mercedes driver was the lead rookie in a session that featured 10 of them; only Ferrari ruined the full-house fun by opting against surrendering one of the SF-26s to a junior driver.

Perhaps the most consequential running came for Colton Herta, who completed 24 laps — and therefore 100km — during the session in Valtteri Bottas' Cadillac.

By doing so, the American earned his FIA Super Licence, taking a considerable step towards his goal of racing in F1.

[Full FP1 report continues below]

Charles Leclerc sends ominous message as Colton Herta takes huge step towards F1 in Mexico FP1

# Driver Team Time Tyre

Results are being loaded...

Opening 30 minutes

The action for a busy FP1 session kicked off immediately when the first hour of running at the Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez began, with the vast majority of the field filing out of the pit lane.

With 10 rookies taking part in the session, all were keen to get as much time on track as possible. Herta, in pursuit of 24 laps to earn his 40th and decisive FIA Super Licence point, pushed his way into the fast lane, with the nine-time IndyCar winner vying for Valtteri Bottas' Cadillac seat, despite a disappointing F2 campaign.

Antonelli, despite having his first push lap deleted for track limits after a messy final sector, led the way early on with an effort in the low 1:20s.

Leclerc brought the hammer down and was quickest as the session reached the one-third distance point, the Ferrari driver putting in a 1:19.197 with Antonelli three tenths off by that stage.

Hadjar was enduring a torrid time of things. Having complained of "something wrong" over team radio, the Frenchman returned to the pits, with his Red Bull seemingly nursing a power unit issue.

Leonardo Fornaroli, deputising for Lando Norris, suffered a huge snap through Turn 11, drifting the McLaren to display impressive car control, having been unsettled by a rival ahead through the tricky esses section.

Numerous drivers experienced moments of their own, including Oscar Piastri in the sister MCL40, who found the grass at Turn 1, doing the floor of his car no favours.

Hamilton, having completed airflow experiments, had the aerodynamic rake removed from his SF-26 for some representative running. The seven-time F1 drivers' immediately slotted into third, seven tenths slower than his team-mate.

Freddie Slater suffered a disastrous half an hour, putting in only six sighter laps, including one with a fan still attached to the right-hand sidepod of his Audi.

That will lead to a fine from the FIA, and it looked to be the reason for the team telling him to switch the engine off when he returned to the garage; his afternoon was over — or so the team suggested.

Second half

Leclerc continued to bring the hammer down, reducing the benchmark to a 1:18.128, beating his — and the session's — best time from FP1 in Mexico 12 months ago, which was a 1:18.380.

Pierre Gasly was enjoying a strong start to his weekend, up in fourth for Alpine with a 1:19.210, just ahead of the leading rookie, Iwasa in Max Verstappen's RB22.

Fred Vesti soon bested the Red Bull driver, slotting in third, less than a tenth of a second slower than Antonelli.

Moments later, another rookie runner, Jak Crawford, was instructed to stop Lance Stroll's Aston Martin, bringing out a virtual safety car.

When the session resumed at full speed, Slater produced somewhat of a plot twist by returning to the fray, with Audi having remedied whatever was ailing his R26.

The British driver eventually popped a time on the board, only quick enough for P21. He also emulated Piastri by running over the grass through the Turns 1-3 complex.

Nikola Tsolov, who was P12 in Liam Lawson's Racing Bulls car, suffered from a dead right leg and had to shake it out before returning to the cockpit and the circuit in the final few minutes. The Bulgarian would have had a complete seat fit and has run in older F1 cars, but is taller than both Lawson and Arvid Lindblad, around whom the VCARB 03 was designed.

Fernando Alonso popped up in seventh, the best finish for Aston Martin in any session all season, underlining the continued progress at the Silverstone-based squad.

In the dying moments, Herta completed his 24th and most important lap, earning himself the final point towards his FIA Super Licence.

title: Colton Herta finally qualifies for crucial F1 document as seat rumours grow
excerpt:
Colton Herta has finally qualified for an FIA superlicence, paving the way for him to potentially graduate to an F1 race seat in 2027.

Herta took over Valtteri Bottas's Cadillac F1 car during Free Practice 1 at the Mexico City Grand Prix, and after completing 24 laps of the Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez, racked up the 100km of running required to earn a point towards his superlicence.

Crucially, this was Herta's 40th superlicence point, meaning he has reached the magic tally required to receive a superlicence and potentially race in F1.

Herta, according to the team, had been on 39 points following his FP1 outing in the United States, with the bulk of these coming in his 2024 IndyCar season, where he achieved 30 points for finishing as runner-up.

The Californian had racked up three extra points through his FP1 outings in Barcelona, Austria, and the United States to take him to 39 points overall, with a Cadillac spokesperson confirming to RacingNews365 that it would be "remiss" not to give him a chance to achieve his superlicence.

Herta had driven Perez's car in another FP1 outing in Italy, but due to technical issues, did not complete the required 100km to earn a point, only managing 25km of running.

This has now been achieved, meaning Herta is now free to race in F1 should he be able to find a seat.

He has made no secret of his desire to race in F1, with a potential path emerging in recent weeks at Cadillac.

Team boss Marcin Budkowski did not immediately shut down rumours of a potential driver swap when questioned in Austin, with the team then re-signing Sergio Perez to a long-term deal until the end of 2029 - with Bottas's future in doubt.

Herta is understood to be a contender for a 2027 F1 race seat if a change is made - with the final hurdle of gaining a superlicence now cleared.

A previous attempt by Herta to race in F1 in 2022 was denied by the FIA. At the time, Helmut Marko was keen to sign him for what was then AlphaTauri, but the request for a waiver to compete without a superlicence was denied.

title: British rookie involved in unusual pit error as Audi to face Mexico City GP stewards
excerpt:
Freddie Slater suffered an F1 debut to forget in first practice for the Mexico City Grand Prix.

Slater, who finished second on his debut in F3 this season, will move up to F2 next season with the front-running Invicta team.

The 18-year-old, who was the first driver to be brought into Audi's driver development programme following the team's entry into F1 this season, is seen as a rising star.

But Slater endured a miserable first practice outing at the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez, driving in place of Gabriel Bortoleto, initially after being sent out on track at one stage with a cooling fan still inside the right-hand sidepod of his car.

Slater was naturally recalled to the pits by Audi to have the fan removed, leading to the stewards to investigate the team after the session for his car being released in an unsafe condition.

On his next lap, Slater was told to return to the pits again, bringing what at the time appeared to be an unfortunately early end to his season as he was told to turn off the engine after pulling into his grid box.

It left Slater with just six laps to his name at that stage, and without a time on the board at the bottom of the timing sheet.

But with just under 11 minutes remaining, whatever was ailing the Audi was fixed, allowing Slater to head back out on track for another opportunity.

On his ninth lap, Slater finally posted a time, 4.3s behind Ferrari driver Charles Leclerc. On his final push lap, he improved to 1:20.945s, 2.817s behind Leclerc, to lift himself off the foot of the times.

Slater will be hoping for an improvement next weekend when he replaces Nick Hulkenberg in FP1 ahead of the São Paulo GP.

title: Every FP1 rookie driver in the 2026 F1 season
excerpt:
As part of the rules to give young, rookie drivers more relevant on-track running, changes were made ahead of 2025.

Previously, teams were required to put a rookie driver in for one FP1 session throughout the year on both cars, for a total of two sessions.

For 2025, this was changed to two times per season per car, for four in total. To qualify, a rookie driver must have started two or fewer grands prix.

Below is a full list of how every team stands with its rookie driver sessions thus far in 2026.

LAST UPDATED: Following the 2026 Mexico City Grand Prix. This article will be updated after every Friday FP1 session where an FP1 driver has stepped in.

McLaren - 3/4

Reigning F2 champion Leonardo Fornaroli has completed all three FP1 sessions for McLaren thus far.

He took over Norris's car in Barcelona and Mexico City, whilst Piastri missed Hungary.

Fornaroli will also take Piastri's MCL40 in Brazil.

Mercedes - 3/4

Mercedes used its first mandatory session for Fred Vesti during FP1 at the Barcelona-Catalunya Grand Prix.

He replaced Kimi Antonelli, who then again stepped out in Hungary with George Russell missing his first in Mexico City, again for Vesti.

Red Bull - 3/4

Red Bull's first FP1 session of the year came for Ayumu Iwasa in Barcelona when he deputised for Isack Hadjar.

Max Verstappen stepped out at the Italian Grand Prix and then again at the Mexico City Grand Prix, leaving Hadjar with just one session left.

Ferrari - 2/4

Like most teams, Ferrari took its first FP1 session in Barcelona, with Dino Beganovic getting the nod in place of Lewis Hamilton.

Beganovic got a second outing in Charles Leclerc's SF-26 at the Austrian GP, meaning both Hamilton and Leclerc must miss one more session each.

Williams - 4/5

Williams has outlined its plan for its FP1 sessions with Luke Browning.

He was due to replace Alex Albon in FP1 in Barcelona, but car problems ruined the run, before Browning moving over to take Carlos Sainz's FW48 in Austria.

Albon then stepped out in Italy and again in Mexico City for Browning's fourth official appearance, but after the Barcelona run was ruined, Sainz will stand down in Brazil.

Racing Bulls - 4/4

With Arvid Lindblad the only rookie on the 2026 F1 grid, he completed his two FP1 sessions in Australia and China as he had not started more than two grands prix.

Liam Lawson missed his first session of the year at the Austrian GP, where Ayumu Iwasa deputised.

Lawson's second session came in favour of Nikola Tsolov at the Mexico City Grand Prix.

Aston Martin - 4/4

Aston Martin was the first team to complete an FP1 session, with this coming in the Japanese Grand Prix at Suzuka.

Jak Crawford stepped in for Fernando Alonso, and the American was back in the AMR26 in Austria, this time taking over Lance Stroll's car.

Crawford took over Alonso's car once again in FP1 at the Belgian GP, leaving only Stroll with one more FP1 session to step out for, which was fulfilled by Crawford in Mexico City.

Haas - 3/4

Esteban Ocon completed the first of his sessions at the Austrian GP, with Ryo Hirakawa jumping into his car.

Oliver Bearman completed his first session in Hungary, leaving both drivers with one more to miss each - with Ocon completing his second in favour of Hirakawa in Mexico City.

Audi - 3/4

Paul Aron took over for Nico Hulkenberg at the Barcelona-Catalunya Grand Prix, which was Audi's first session of the year.

Gabriel Bortoleto handed over duties in Austria, with the team deciding to give Freddie Slater his F1 weekend debut in Mexico City, in favour of Bortoleto.

Slater will take Hulkenberg's car in Brazil.

Alpine - 3/4

Alpine's first session of the year came with Franco Colapinto being benched for Paul Aron in Hungary. He must miss one more session.

Pierre Gasly missed the first of his two sessions in Italy, again for Aron.

Colapinto stepped out in Mexico City to hand Gabriele Mini his weekend debut.

Cadillac - 5/5

In Barcelona, Colton Herta finally made his F1 weekend debut, taking Sergio Perez's MAC-26 for a drive.

Perez stepped out for the second time in Italy, with Valtteri Bottas, who handed over his car to Herta in Hungary, requiring one more session.

However, Herta was given the nod for the United States FP1 session, but in Perez's car for the third time. Rules dictate that each of the two regular drivers must step out twice, meaning Bottas must do so in Mexico City, Sao Paulo, Las Vegas, Qatar, or Abu Dhabi.

Bottas did this in Mexico City, meaning Herta finally qualified for his superlicence.

title: Ralf Schumacher involved in scary plane incident: 'Police, fire brigade arrived'
excerpt:
Ralf Schumacher was among the passengers on board a Lufthansa flight which aborted its take-off from Frankfurt Airport on Wednesday following a burst tyre.

The former F1 driver turned pundit was travelling on Lufthansa flight LH1264, an Airbus A320-200 registered D-AIZA, which was bound for Salzburg when the nose-gear tyre failed during the take-off run on October 28 from runway 18.

The flight-deck crew aborted the take-off before the critical V1 rotation speed, after which time, the aircraft would have been forced to take to the air, with a maximum speed reached of 72 knots, according to FlightRadar24.

The aircraft was then met by emergency personnel before being towed back to a gate where the 153 passengers and crew disembarked safely.

Schumacher detailed the drama in a post on Instagram.

"We were already on the runway, at full speed, and then one of the two front tyres burst. Then, of course, there was an emergency stop here in Frankfurt at the airport. The braking was very hard,” he said.

"Police, fire brigade, and all sorts of other emergency services arrived, of course.”

"The crew did a great job. Everything was very, very good.

"A big thank you to Lufthansa. It was great how they handled things for us. The way we were welcomed and immediately rebooked, everything was just perfect. Thanks!"

title: Liam Lawson facing 'cruel' Racing Bulls scenario as F1 future speculation grows
excerpt:
Martin Brundle believes it would be "very cruel" if Liam Lawson and Arvid Lindblad are not racing for Racing Bulls next season, as speculation grows that Red Bull junior Nikola Tsolov could be drafted in for 2027.

The futures of Lawson and Lindblad remain in the air as the end of the current campaign draws near, with Racing Bulls again facing a situation of three-into-two does not go regarding its available race seats for next year.

Lawson would seemingly deserve to be retained after performing admirably at Red Bull for a three-race stint after the summer break in place of the injured Isack Hadjar, whilst he is also comfortably the leading driver in the standings outside of the 'big four' teams in Mercedes, Ferrari, McLaren and Red Bull.

Tsolov, second in the F2 standings with two rounds remaining - should they go ahead in Qatar and Abu Dhabi - has impressed in private testing, whilst former Red Bull motorsport advisor Helmut Marko has publicly backed the Bulgarian over Lawson, arguing the team should stick to its policy of promoting young talent.

Asked by Sky Sports F1 whether Lawson had done enough to keep his seat, Brundle said he believed the 24-year-old deserved to stay. "You'd imagine so, wouldn't you?" he said.

"But in this game, you get your chance because somebody else gets kicked out, and as soon as you get that chance, you're looking over your shoulder if you're not careful.

"But it would seem very cruel if Liam Lawson and Arvid Lindblad are not in those two cars next year. Liam's really found his way. These are complex cars, complex races.

"If I'm honest, the young drivers benefit from not being frightened to death by Dr Helmut Marko every time they get out of the car."

[Article continues below]

Brundle - 'Youngsters need breathing space'

When it was put to Brundle that Marko had already suggested Racing Bulls should turn to Tsolov, he replied: "There you go then, already.

"As you know, Dr Helmut Marko would also say, 'Hang on a minute! I found [Sebastian] Vettel, I found [Daniel] Ricciardo, I found [Max] Verstappen. Tell me which bit of that I got wrong.'

"But I do think the youngsters who come through need some breathing space to make their mistakes, but yes, Tsolov is knocking on the door."

Marko stepped down from his motorsport advisor role at the end of last season, with driver selection now understood to run through a wider group, including Red Bull team principal Laurent Mekies and Racing Bulls counterpart Alan Permane.

Gwen Lagrue, who spent 11 years heading up Mercedes' junior driver operation, joins Red Bull next year as director of the junior programme, effectively replacing Marko.

No decision on the 2027 Racing Bulls line-up has yet been confirmed.

title: Oliver Bearman shares F1 future update amid Haas contract silence
excerpt:
Oliver Bearman has insisted his “goal” is to continue with Haas for the 2027 season, despite the lack of communication about his future.

Bearman is enduring his second full season with the American squad but remains part of the Ferrari team through its driver academy.

Haas has already announced one-half of its line-up for 2027, with rookie Rafael Camara coming in to replace Esteban Ocon, whose exit from the outfit has been confirmed.

It has been expected for some time that Bearman will continue with the team into next year, but the Briton has stated matters are still being finalised.

“No, I think it's very clear,” Bearman told media including RacingNews365.

“I want to continue with Haas. That's definitely my goal.

“There are a few things in the background that we're working on, but it's been very clear that continuing with Haas will be my target, and we're just finalising a few things on that front.”

[Article continues below]

Bearman admits situation 'not in my hands'

Bearman has bagged 23 points so far this year and sits 13th in the drivers' standings, a handful of positions higher than his experienced team-mate Esteban Ocon.

The 21-year-old has only been able to add to his tally once in the last 13 rounds, but has been hindered by the performance struggles endured by Haas.

When asked when he expects an announcement will be made regarding his future, Bearman said: “I don't know, to be honest.

“It's not really in my hands, I can tell you that. If it was up to me, it would have already been announced a long time ago.

“But there are a few bigger-picture things that we're working on.”

title: Sergio Perez to miss key Mexico City Grand Prix event through illness
excerpt:
Sergio Pérez has pulled out of his home fan forum in Mexico City after falling ill on the morning of his home grand prix weekend.

The 36-year-old was due to greet supporters at the event ahead of first practice at the Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez, but the team opted to give him extra time to recover rather than risk his condition worsening before the track sessions.

Cadillac released a statement explaining the decision, which also addressed the impact on Pérez's weekend schedule.

"Checo Pérez will unfortunately be unable to attend today's fan forum at his home grand prix due to illness," read the statement. "Both he and the team apologise to all the fans who have come out to see him.

"Checo and the team have taken the decision to allow him additional time to rest and recover this morning, ahead of today's on-track sessions.

"His participation in the remainder of the race weekend, including FP1 and FP2, is not affected.

"We thank our fans for their understanding and support and look forward to seeing you on track."

Pérez is not the only Cadillac driver to have been troubled by illness this week. Team-mate Valtteri Bottas withdrew from his media duties on Thursday after also falling unwell.

But the Finn has since been declared fit to take part, with Cadillac confirming he was given the all-clear this morning to join second practice.

title: Red Bull unleash latest upgrade as F1 development war set for extreme test
excerpt:
Red Bull is the only front-running team to bring upgrades to the Mexico City Grand Prix, submitting an upgraded engine cover and revised sidepod for this weekend's round at the Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez.

The Milton Keynes-based squad has registered a reworked engine cover and new sidepod design, according to the FIA's car presentation documents.

Red Bull's new engine cover features an increased exit area to recover cooling mass flow through the radiators, achieved by extending the area of the existing louvres and adding optional louvres further outboard.

As for the new cooling sidepod design, the sidepod itself carries an adapted split line to match a revised floor surface behind the outer fence, aimed at recovering small aerodynamic gains while improving heat rejection.

Cooling is at a premium in Mexico City. Sitting more than 2,200 metres above sea level, the circuit exposes cars to around 20 to 25 per cent less ambient air density than at sea-level venues, drastically cutting the mass airflow through radiators and heat exchangers.

That thinner air also means larger cooling cutouts carry less of an aerodynamic drag penalty than they would elsewhere on the calendar, making the altitude race one of the few windows where teams can justify opening up bodywork without a lap-time trade-off.

The altitude in Mexico City is one of the most extreme tests on the F1 calendar, even more so with the new power unit regulations.

Audi has introduced an upgraded rear brake duct deflector, while Alpine has a new exhaust tailpipe. Ferrari, McLaren and Racing Bulls are the only three teams to introduce parts specific to Mexico City's demands.

title: Kimi Antonelli and Valtteri Bottas medical update after being hit with illness
excerpt:
Kimi Antonelli and Valtteri Bottas have both been cleared to take part in practice for the Mexico City Grand Prix after illness forced them to miss their media commitments on Thursday.

Antonelli, who can secure the F1 drivers' title this weekend, was excused from all mandatory Thursday media sessions at the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez while recovering from a viral illness, with Mercedes confirming the Italian's absence had been approved as a precaution.

Bottas, meanwhile, skipped his own Thursday duties after feeling unwell, with Cadillac granting him a rest day to aid his recovery rather than disclosing a specific diagnosis.

Under FIA regulations, any driver who falls ill at a grand prix weekend must be assessed by team medical staff before being signed off as fit to drive by the FIA Medical Delegate at the circuit medical centre.

Both Antonelli and Bottas have now gone through that process and been given the all-clear to appear in Friday's running.

A Mercedes spokesperson confirmed the 20-year-old Antonelli has recovered in time for FP1, stating: "He's all good and so will be in the car today."

Bottas will resume his normal weekend programme in Mexico City for FP2, with the Finn making way for Colton Herta, who is poised to complete enough laps that will see him finally acquire his FIA Super Licence.

A Cadillac statement read: "Valtteri will fulfil all media duties and take part in free practice 2 today as planned.

Neither driver's illness is understood to carry any lasting fitness concerns heading into the rest of the weekend, though it remains unclear exactly what symptoms triggered their absences in the first place.

title: George Russell offers two reasons for wildly inconsistent season as defeat looms
excerpt:
George Russell has pointed to two factors he believes could be responsible for his wildly inconsistent season, which is now entering its end-game.

Should Russell or his nearest rival Lewis Hamilton fail to win the Mexico City Grand Prix, then Russell's team-mate Kimi Antonelli will be crowned champion in just his second season of grand prix racing - and become the youngest-ever title winner.

Even if Russell does win the race, Antonelli would only require a ninth-place finish to become the 36th F1 champion, as the Italian's coronation looks set for Sunday's race.

Russell had started the season in dominant fashion with pole and victory in Australia before Antonelli went on a run of five straight wins to open a points gap he has never relinquished.

Although Russell has been able to produce strong weekends, including in Azerbaijan with a grand chelem, he has finished off the podium seven times compared to twice for Antonelli - one of which was caused by his wheel shield failure during the British GP and resulting time penalties for track limits.

As defeat beckons for Russell, the Briton, who has been vocal about his driving style impacting his performance, offered fascinating insight into his struggles and how the car underneath him was working against him.

"I think there have been quite a few factors with the cars this year that potentially favour or hinder a certain driving style," Russell began to media, including RacingNews365.

"I've always been a driver that focuses on the mid to the exit of the corners, which often means I'm on the throttle earlier than most.

"And with these new power units, that means I'm spending more energy, and it's sometimes not the most efficient way to drive for the power unit.

"Secondly, the tyre pressures this year, especially on the rear, have been very, very high.

"Pirelli have taken a few PSI of margin, especially on the rear axle, and so that has sort of hindered me by pushing on the exits, as the rear tyres can't cope with it as well.

"And then there's been the hindrance on the power unit side, so these two factors just really hampered my natural driving style, and I'd say that's probably been the biggest thing of this season."

[Article continues below]

Russell defiant over tough season

Such has been the volatility of the tough season; Russell labelled the situation as "quite strange" as he explained the "confusion" he and his engineers were finding themselves in.

"I mean, if we had the answer, maybe I'd be able to maybe replicate it more often, and that's been part of the challenge this year and some of the confusion," he continued.

"I came out of Monaco, and it was a very difficult weekend for me, and I went to Barcelona and was quickest in every session, and put it on pole. Went to Austria at the next race, was on pole again, and then a few races later, I was qualifying down in P5 and P6.

"In Baku, I was on pole by eight tenths and in Malaysia, I think I qualified P8.

"I feel in the years gone by, I had a pretty high hit rate of reaching the potential of the car, and maybe at the end of the season, there were four or five races, I feel that were not maximised.

"I remember 2022. We finished in the top five more than any other driver in the whole season; I think it was 19 from 22 races, and this was the third best car on the grid.

"And now this season we have the best car, and I'm not able to achieve these results, so it's quite strange, and we're certainly scratching our heads a little bit, and it's definitely not through a lack of trying."

title: The 10 F1 rookies who will drive during Mexico City FP1
excerpt:
The opening practice session of the Mexico City Grand Prix weekend will feature 10 rookies during the 60-minute outing.

As per Article B1.7.3 of the sporting regulations, F1 teams are required to provide two practice outings per car during the season to give experience to rookie drivers.

The Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez has proven to be a popular location to do so this year, with Ferrari being the only squad not to nominate a substitute for the opening practice segment.

At the front of the field, Fred Vesti will once again jump behind the wheel, standing in for George Russell in what will be his seventh FP1 appearance.

Reigning Formula 2 champion Leonardo Fornaroli will climb aboard the McLaren for the third time this year, while Ayumu Iwasa will have another appearance at Red Bull.

There will be three FP1 debutants on Friday - Nikola Tsolov for Racing Bulls, Freddie Slater for Audi and Gabriele Mini for Alpine.

Luke Browning will have another outing with Williams, while Jak Crawford and Ryo Hirakawa will fulfil duties at Aston Martin and Haas, respectively.

Finally, Colton Herta is having another go at Cadillac, and depending on his mileage during the session, he could finally be eligible to pick up a super licence required to race in F1.
